title: Compatibility translation: runtime deviation analysis and mitigation action log
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: Investigate concrete runtime-level deviations introduced by the compatibility translation layer that maps OpenAI Responses semantics to Redwood's internal streaming + tool-calling model. Deliverables: a prioritized gap catalog (behavioral diffs with examples), a small experiment matrix that tests streaming chunk boundaries, tool call scoping, structured output shape fidelity, and a mitigation playbook with telemetry detectors and canary rollout configs. Scope excludes broad protocol redesigns; focus is on pragmatic runtime adapters and short-term fallbacks to preserve customer SLAs.
acceptance_criteria: Comprehensive catalog of >= 25 reproducible behavior deltas between OpenAI Responses and Redwood runtime with example requests and expected vs observed outputs
Telemetry hooks instrumented to surface the top 5 drift signals (stream boundary mismatches, truncated structured fields, tool-call omission, event ordering, token provenance) in staging

Two mitigation patterns implemented and canaried: (1) event-resequencer for out-of-order stream events, (2) structured-output normalizer that preserves absent/extra fields and emits a compatibility header
Runbooks updated and public internal doc with rollback thresholds and automated fallback to golden-response proxy
work_breakdown_steps: Discovery: fuzz test corpus generation from representative customer prompts (privacy-scrubbed)
Instrumentation: add streaming event annotations and token provenance IDs to staging only
Analysis: run diff harness comparing OpenAI reference responses against Redwood conversion for streaming+toolcall cases
Prototype mitigations: implement resequencer middleware and structured normalizer in the translation path
Canary: deploy mitigations behind feature flag to 5% of traffic and monitor and alert
Docs & Runbook: produce remediation steps, SLOs, and customer communications templates
discussion: 2025-01-10 - AP: Kickoff review with PM and Design. PM asked for customer-facing severity buckets (none/low/med/high) and for a narrow canary plan before major changes.

2025-01-15 - LO: Implemented initial streaming annotations. Observed that function-call end-of-call markers are sometimes emitted as separate events in OpenAI responses, causing our tool router to treat them as two calls. Created spike ENG-581312-SPK for routing fix exploration.
2025-01-28 - AP: Design feedback - structured outputs should include a compatibility metadata envelope instead of flattening to avoid breaking strict JSON schema consumers.
2025-02-04 - LO: Telemetry prototype pushed (PR #4821). Early dashboards show three signal spikes when the client uses chunked transfer encoding with small chunk sizes.
2025-02-12 - PM: Decision to prioritize resequencer middleware over aggressive structural rewriting to minimize behavioral changes for customers with strict schemas.
2025-02-18 - LO: Canary started (5%). No P0 regressions so far; two P1 alerts for truncated structured fields logged and automatically backfilled by normalizer in 92% of cases. Continuing canary.
status_updates: 2025-01-20 - In Progress: Discovery complete, instrumentation merged to staging.
2025-02-04 - In Progress: Analysis complete; gap catalog draft (26 items) available in Confluence.
2025-02-18 - In Progress: Mitigations deployed behind FF; canary started at 5% traffic.
2025-02-20 - In Progress: Canary healthy, expanding to 15% for additional telemetry sampling.
decision_log: Prefer non-invasive middleware (resequencer + normalizer) rather than altering the canonical runtime event model to preserve existing customers.
Emit a compatibility envelope header for structured outputs instead of changing JSON payload shape by default; allow opt-in strict mode.
Use token provenance IDs to correlate stream fragments with tool calls and enable automated reconciliation.
Initial canary safely limited to 5% with automated rollback on >3 P0s in 1h window.
fallback_strategy: Feature-flagged automatic fallback to golden-response proxy (a lightweight translator that replays OpenAI events) for sessions that fail normalizer heuristics
Client-visible X-Compat-Warning header emitted when normalization modifies payload shape
Fallback activation requires fewer than 2% of total requests per customer to be eligible to avoid amplification
notes: Risk: aggressive normalization might hide upstream model behavioral regressions; prefer explicit telemetry and customer opt-in for destructive fixes.
Next steps: expand canary to 15% (2025-02-21), then trigger a staged rollout with QA signoff if no P0s for 24h.
